title: Beyond columnwise controls: finite certificates and routing bounds
body:
Cross-column routing, changing representations and approximate consumers sit outside many existing native-control obstructions. This contribution gives a usable **finite-memory physical endpoint contract**: a fixed transfer table either has an exact certificate for every positive width or a literal counterexample at bounded width. It also proves exponential transfer-dimension requirements for two routing families, including operator-norm approximation.

The [proof](https://github.com/zxv/integer-mult-bounds/blob/11fedb46fa199283f78282187c10aea432d8b0bb/research/finite-memory-lifting/PROOF.md) and [research guide](https://github.com/zxv/integer-mult-bounds/blob/11fedb46fa199283f78282187c10aea432d8b0bb/research/finite-memory-lifting/README.md) develop the scope, constructions and follow-ups. This is a scoped written theorem with author-checked exact tools, awaiting independent mathematical review. The automata and matrix-product foundations are classical; no new general equivalence algorithm, global literature priority, paid-query minimum or κ is claimed.

## Result

Let a complete residual endpoint have entries

```math
\left[F\,T_{(y_1,x_1)}\cdots T_{(y_f,x_f)}\,B\right]_{
  \text{output role},\,\text{input role}},
```

with **fixed $`D`$-state transitions and boundaries**, including every independent input and required dirty return. Then it vanishes at all positive widths **iff it vanishes at every width $`1,\ldots,D`$**. A $`D`$-cycle first fails exactly at width $`D`$, so the bound is sharp. The proof refines it to $`D-r_1+1`$ when the positive seed space has rank $`r_1\gt 0`$.

The tool avoids constructing those tensor matrices. It emits a finite invariant-row certificate

```math
F T_s=E_sR,\qquad R T_s=C_sR,\qquad RB=0
\quad\text{for every physical column pair }s.
```

Alternatively, it emits a physical input/output column, role pair and exact nonzero discrepancy. A separately transcribed checker performs only exact equations or literal witness replay; it imports no producer or elimination code.

| Consequence | Scope and practical use |
|---|---|
| **Concrete all-width semantics** | Physical column entries already contain native relations and absolute phases. Dense/non-Clifford maps and finite-memory column mixing are allowed. All entries and return roles matter; sampled widths/columns are insufficient. |
| **Compositional contracts** | Sums add transfer dimensions; physical compositions multiply them, with global owner sums handled separately. Supplied recurrence coefficients $`aG^fb`$ and finite schedule/width filters are included in the state bound. |
| **A strict cross-column extension** | Prefix XOR has minimum transfer dimension two and a certified inverse. It does not commute with column permutations, so identical one-column tensor-power expansions cannot represent it. This extends the semantic scope beyond [#5436](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5436). |
| **A pinned native adapter** | The [nine-axis source word](https://github.com/zxv/integer-mult-bounds/blob/11fedb46fa199283f78282187c10aea432d8b0bb/research/finite-memory-lifting/SOURCE-FIXTURE.json) from [#5369](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5369) is checked with both dirty roles, all four owner/input blocks and all 512 local addresses. Its prefix-encoded shear has eight transfer states and a two-row invariant. |
| **Exact and robust routing exclusions** | Swapping two $`k`$-column halves of local dimension $`d`$ requires $`D\ge d^{2k}`$; their complex phase $`(-1)^{a\cdot b}`$ requires $`D\ge 2^k`$. Operator-norm error $`\varepsilon\lt 1`$ still requires $`D\ge(1-\varepsilon^2)d^{2k}`$ and $`D\ge(1-\varepsilon^2)2^k`$, respectively. These are cut-rank bounds in the declared column order. |
| **Sharp limits on testing** | Bounded bond separately at each width does not imply a fixed-table family. Small early-width errors do not imply a uniform approximation bound, even for fixed unitary families with a two-state comparison. |

## Significance for researchers

This opens a verifiable class of changed column interfaces and closes bounded-transfer-state searches for specific nonlocal routing demands. A proposal can yield either a complete all-width certificate, a concrete semantic defect, or a finite cut-rank obstruction before expensive physical synthesis. For [#5419](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5419)'s changed consumers and [#5427](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5427)'s observation questions, the next task becomes precise: extract the actual physical tables with source versions and returns. This package has not supplied a missing observation or decided those callers.

## Risks and tradeoffs

| Boundary | Opportunity and remaining obligation |
|---|---|
| **Transfer dimension is a representation cost** | Small $`D`$ can make exact checking cheap. It does not price owned fields, physical memory, Gaussian calls, column access or tape movement. A virtual two-state map is not a free native primitive. |
| **Extraction can expand** | Closure checking is polynomial in the explicit table. Extracting that table from a succinct program can grow exponentially; existing formal/native frontends may be much smaller. |
| **Uniformity is essential** | Arbitrary width-dependent boundaries, recipes or position schedules invalidate the cutoff unless a fixed finite controller is explicitly included. Regular restrictions prove only their declared domain. |
| **Inverses and dirty state** | A supplied inverse must have a valid representation and complete endpoint checks. Bounded representation of an arbitrary inverse is not assumed. Returning zero cannot replace restoration of an independent dirty input. |
| **Routing and approximation** | The bounds depend on the cut and column order; legal reordering or side information may change them. The signed-phase/norm bounds use complex semantics, not $`\mathbb{F}_2`$/BIT. Exact certificates do not supply recovery-safe precision bounds. |
| **Source and proof status** | The source instance is a nine-axis identity, not the full provider or selected caller. Independent review, physical compilation, pricing, precision, stock and analytic transfer remain open. |

## Nearest overlapping work

| Relevant work | Retained contribution and distinction |
|---|---|
| [#5235](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5235), [#5262](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5262), [#5352](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5352) | Classical automata-based complete register certificates, true named inverses and bit bounds. Their alphabet is formal operator letters; here it is concrete physical input/output column pairs, with a fixed finite-memory family across widths. |
| [#5369](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5369), [#2250](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2250) | Specialized affine-quadratic native lifting and the recipe lineage. The source fixture is retained exactly. Their compact specialized criterion remains preferable within its language. |
| [#5436](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5436) | Moving-support columnwise obstruction. Prefix XOR supplies a concrete map outside that representation; the current theorem requires fixed finite transfer tables instead of its pointwise support hypothesis. |
| [#5419](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5419), [#5427](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5427) | Changed coupled consumers and frozen-word observation/reuse tests. They motivate source adapters; their availability, price and physical nonmembership claims are not promoted through this theorem. |
| [#5425](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5425) | Standalone paid-fanout optimum in its stated grammar. Transfer dimension and cut rank do not extend that result to incremental costs at a caller cut. |

Classical inputs retain credit to [weighted-automata equivalence](https://people.mpi-sws.org/~joel/publications/Q_weighted_automata13.pdf), [Tzeng's algorithm](https://doi.org/10.1137/0221017) and [the matrix-product/automata correspondence](https://arxiv.org/abs/0708.1221). Cut-rank and projection-error arguments are also classical. The new contribution is this concrete repository contract, source-bound frontend and explicit enabling/exclusion boundaries.

## Validation

```sh
python3 -B research/finite-memory-lifting/verify.py
python3 -O -B research/finite-memory-lifting/verify.py
python3 -B research/finite-memory-lifting/audit_mutations.py
python3 -B research/finite-memory-lifting/verify.py --source-root .
```

- **24 small transfer tables**, 138 independent path-sum comparisons, and sharp first-failure examples at widths 1 through 12.
- **126 literal prefix/inverse columns and 340 complete prefix matrix entries**, with a nonzero cut minor and a five-state inverse residual certificate.
- All **four dirty owner/input blocks**, **512 independent native address checks**, an eight-state encoded shear and a rejecting absolute-phase mutation.
- Exact half-swap unfoldings through width eight, Walsh cut/Gram controls through width twelve, and fixed-unitary examples with small early but large late errors.
- Ten invalid-certificate/input controls and four semantic code mutations in normal/optimized modes. Standalone checker runs without the producer, Git or PATH tools; portable read-only replay preserves source bytes.

[RESULT.json](https://github.com/zxv/integer-mult-bounds/blob/11fedb46fa199283f78282187c10aea432d8b0bb/research/finite-memory-lifting/RESULT.json), [VALIDATION.json](https://github.com/zxv/integer-mult-bounds/blob/11fedb46fa199283f78282187c10aea432d8b0bb/research/finite-memory-lifting/VALIDATION.json) and [MUTATIONS.json](https://github.com/zxv/integer-mult-bounds/blob/11fedb46fa199283f78282187c10aea432d8b0bb/research/finite-memory-lifting/MUTATIONS.json) retain the outputs and actual environment. [SOURCES.json](https://github.com/zxv/integer-mult-bounds/blob/11fedb46fa199283f78282187c10aea432d8b0bb/research/finite-memory-lifting/SOURCES.json) pins seven canonical provenance files at [`32890bc`](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04), priority revision 7; selected conditional $`\kappa=0.003027288235`$. [OVERLAP.json](https://github.com/zxv/integer-mult-bounds/blob/11fedb46fa199283f78282187c10aea432d8b0bb/research/finite-memory-lifting/OVERLAP.json) states bounded coverage, including its historical/local limitations.

No full 112-owner/17-axis provider, selected cold replay, physical cross-column implementation, generic replay registration, Lean, Docker or hosted CI run is claimed. Universal conclusions rest on the written proof.

## Open next questions

| Investigation | First useful result and principal blocker |
|---|---|
| **One actual caller** | Extract complete physical transfer tables for a named provider/consumer, with source versions and dirty returns. Table/state growth may defeat direct extraction. |
| **Physical observation membership** | Bind one candidate from [#5427](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5427) to actual phases and entries. Formal-word nonmembership alone does not answer this. |
| **A legal column-mixing adapter** | Price prefix encoding, its inverse, access and restoration in an allowed native/tape contract. Virtual state count does not supply the bill. |
| **Source-specific cut obstructions** | Produce one exact coefficient minor for a real routing demand, after allowing legal reordering and side information. A convenient artificial cut is insufficient. |
| **Compact semantic extraction** | Combine the existing formal frontends with physical transfer tables and polynomial bit certificates. Concrete relations can cause state explosion. |
| **Uniform approximation and recovery** | Prove a conditioning/contractivity criterion for a real consumer, then account for precision and exact recovery. Early-width tolerance checks cannot certify it. |
